analysis.title: The Point for North America, Monday, 16 November 2026
key_insights: Hardware C3Q26 previews: Citi expects strong enterprise infrastructure OEM results on a broad refresh cycle (Citi 3Q CIO survey, VAR checks, OEM and supply chain comments). AI infrastructure demand looks robust per SMCI, CoreWeave, TSMC and Wistron commentary. Peak-AI-demand and 'over-earning' fears (pull-forward demand, stabilizing memory prices) compressed multiples and share prices during the quarter. PCs weakened on negative IDC data and Intel earnings. Prefers DELL, HPE and P (constructive).

Software Playbook for 2027: more selective stance as investors demand tangible AI adoption, monetization and estimate upside. Favors infrastructure, data and security vendors with direct AI workload exposure. Top ideas: MDB, SNOW, ESTC, NET, TEAM, DDOG, BOX, NAVN, ROP.

Citi views post-midterm data center concerns as a sentiment and positioning risk, not a change in long-term AI demand. AI disruption to traditional search creates top-of-funnel pressure for SMB and self-service software vendors, warranting caution. Renewed strategic M&A should support valuations for scarce AI, data, security and workflow assets.

Appian (APPN): investor meetings with management showed continued legacy modernization demand. Management pushes back on AI-displacement fears and says enterprises will not trust mission-critical workflows to vibe-coded apps. New Enterprise Growth Plans and added sales capacity support the growth outlook. Reiterate Buy/High Risk.

Summit Therapeutics (SMMT): model updated for the 2L EGFR NSCLC complete response letter. That indication was valued at 35% probability of success, about $300M peak risk-adjusted revenue and about $1/share. Thesis rests on the H-3 final PFS readout in early 1Q27. TP $42 (from $43). Buy/High Risk.

EOG Resources: 3Q had an in-line CFPS beat, a modest production guide raise and an 8% dividend increase. UAE exploration results point toward commerciality, with some production in 2027 and most impact in 2028 and later. A ~$300mm Janus expansion doubles processing capacity, with completion in 2H28. Stock trades at a premium, so exploration is the catalyst to monitor. Neutral, TP $155 (from $150).

Roblox (RBLX) downgraded to Neutral from Buy. Reasons: Steal An Egg popularity has waned, no new hit among the top 10 experiences, possible GTA VI risk (launches November 19), and 4Q26 bookings likely just below the guide midpoint. TP unchanged at $55.

Nebius (NBIS): solid Q3 beat, but near-term revenue guidance was trimmed on site delays at Vineland NJ and multiple third-party sites. Prepayments now cover more than 100% of associated capex. Citi's FY27 revenue estimates rise 14pts while EPS estimates fall 19pts. Buy/High Risk, TP $215 (from $265).

EchoStar (ECHO): 3Q reported without a call. DISH DBS emerged from bankruptcy 10/2/26, while Hughes and DISH Wireless remain in court. Possible catalysts: monetizing AWS-3 paired spectrum before the 1/20/27 auction registration deadline, and a DISH DBS monetization via a DTV merger or privatization. Buy/High Risk, TP $139 (from $117).

DTE Energy: management meeting points to a likely third, smaller datacenter deal by YE26 and a short datacenter pause in 2027. EPS outlook above 9% through 2031, backed by a $44.2B capex plan and a ~$3B Vantage sale. Large load tariff decision and electric case are upcoming.

Cerebras (CBRS) beat its Sep-Q guide on all core metrics and raised FY26 core revenue to $940M-$960M. Dec-Q guide of $310M-$330M came well above Street, helped by new hardware orders including Oracle. Initial key customer tranches are behind schedule on land, power and building shells. Announced a cloud deal with MSFT. TP cut to $250 from $320 on 7x EV/S vs 14x prior. Buy.

Rivian (RIVN): nine-month revenue up 27% to $5.2B, driven by Amazon and the VW JV. Consumer unit-sale revenue fell 18% vs a 29% drop in US BEV industry sales. Citi expects a $1.7B EBITDA loss in 2026. YE cash of $5.5B gives liquidity into mid-2028. Neutral, TP $14.50 (from $18).

Veradermics (MANE) and Beam (BEAM): MANE male program is seen as substantially de-risked, with female Study 306 data in 1H27 the next catalyst (Buy/High Risk, $175 TP). Beam's PKU franchise is viewed as underappreciated, with the risto-cel SCD BLA filing possible as early as YE26.
Back Office Software rankings: top picks BOX, NAVN, ROP. Ranking changes: down APPN and MANH on valuation, up ROP and PCTY on execution, down INTU and MNDY on SMB top-of-funnel concerns.

Waste Services: coverage up 9.6% over 30 days on solid 3Q results, early 2027 details and rotation. Citi expects firm pricing next year as CPI accelerating from March to September passes through on a ~12-month lag. CLH has the highest crowding rank at 0.95 (composite 0.96 vs prior); CWST the lowest at 0.13.

Utilities EEI takeaways: data center growth continues in states that can address public opposition. Growth acceleration visible in Arizona, West Virginia, Wisconsin, Indiana and Florida. Citi is more positive on FE, AEP, PNW, ES, MDU and PEG.

Construction economists see data center and mega-project activity as the market's engine, though with a more cautious tone. Data center starts are up 173% YTD. Policy risk would hit 2028 spending more than 2027. A broad non-residential and residential recovery may not come until 2H27.

AI: Google acquired a pre-developed Wyoming site, showing the hyperscaler balance-sheet edge. OpenRouter token count rose 8% WoW to 210T. Meta's Muse Ember scores 8 points below Muse Wonder on the AA Index at about 1/50th of the cost. eBay reportedly blocks third-party agents.

PULSE Monitor: NVDA's 37% retrenchment over five weeks has dragged the S&P 500 down by about 200bps. Citi compares it to AAPL circa 2018 but hesitates to draw the analogy yet. Q3 earnings show better positive surprise breadth, though noise is rising for the AI-attached cohort. Growth cluster forward PE is 18.3x, now below Defensives.
Midterms: Democrats won majorities in both House and Senate, with cost of living and AI backlash cited. Divided government makes a dramatic shift in US policy trajectory unlikely.

US Economics: October PPI final demand rose 0.3% MoM, core PPI (ex food, energy, trade services) rose 0.5%, core goods rose 0.55% MoM (strongest since May), concentrated in electronics and computers on AI demand. Airfares and medical services were weaker than expected. Citi lowered its October core PCE estimate to 0.27% MoM and 3.2% YoY.

US Rates: Citi stays neutral duration because front-end tail risks lean to the upside after the inflation print and hawkish Fedspeak. Long 30y TIPS breakevens is the preferred implicit short-duration trade. Citi adds to its 1x2 SOFR H7 put spread (95.5/95.25) to hedge tail risk of multiple rate hikes and is short upper-left vol.
